title: HF14 (2023-2024 Regular): Criminal background checks required for firearms transfers, and grounds for disqualification of transferee permit modified.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (2nd Engrossment, 2023-02-13; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/HF/14/versions/2/)
provenance.note: Version read: 2nd Engrossment, 2023-02-13 (revisor.mn.gov). Struck passages (old seven-day/five-business-day periods, old sole-basis disqualification, old unknown-party ID rule, old gross misdemeanor for false statement, transfer-report exemption for permit holders) are not quoted. Adds a criminal-gang-database ground and 30-day periods, and lets a licensed dealer run the check. No vote data on file; amendments made after this version are not in the text read.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4): The chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a transferee permit if the applicant is: (1) prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon; (2) determined to be a danger to self or the public when in possession of firearms under paragraph (b); or (3) listed in the criminal gang investigative data system under section 299C.091.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4): A chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a permit to a person if there exists a substantial likelihood that the applicant is a danger to self or the public when in possession of a firearm.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 5): The chief of police or sheriff shall issue a transferee permit or deny the application within 30 days of application for the permit.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 11): A person who makes a false statement in order to obtain a transferee permit knowing or having reason to know the statement is false is guilty of a felony.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 4): Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 7 or 8, no person shall deliver a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to a proposed transferee until 30 days after the date the agreement to transfer is delivered to a chief of police or sheriff in accordance with subdivision 1 unless the chief of police or sheriff waives all or a portion of the waiting period.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): An unlicensed person is prohibited from transferring a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to any other unlicensed person, unless: (1) the transfer is made through a firearms dealer as provided for in subdivision 3; or (2) the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): If the transferee is prohibited by federal law from purchasing or possessing the firearm or not entitled under state law to possess the firearm, neither the federally licensed firearms dealer nor the transferor shall transfer the firearm to the transferee.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 5): A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.
